questions.title: Reaction Speed
questions.question: How quickly do your allergy symptoms typically begin around cats?
questions.subtitle: Immediate reactions indicate higher circulating IgE antibodies to airborne Fel d 1.

options.label: I rarely or never notice immediate symptoms
options.description: Even after prolonged contact or visiting homes with cats.

options.label: After several hours or prolonged cuddling
options.description: Symptoms only develop after heavy direct contact with a cat.

options.label: Within 30 to 60 minutes of entering a cat-occupied room
options.description: Sneezing or eye itching begins as airborne dander circulates.

options.label: Almost instantly upon entering a home with a cat
options.description: Rapid reaction even before touching or seeing the feline.

questions.title: Nasal & Sinus Reactions
questions.question: How severely do nasal and sinus symptoms affect you around cats?
questions.subtitle: Allergic rhinitis is the most common manifestation of feline protein exposure.

options.label: None or negligible
options.description: No noticeable sneezing, congestion, or runny nose.

options.label: Mild sniffle or occasional sneeze
options.description: Minor irritation that fades naturally and does not impede daily activities.

options.label: Frequent sneezing, stuffed nose, or post-nasal drip
options.description: Continuous nasal congestion that requires blowing your nose repeatedly.

options.label: Uncontrollable sneezing fits, complete nasal blockage, sinus headache
options.description: Severe airway inflammation causing painful facial pressure and fatigue.

questions.title: Eye Irritation
questions.question: What happens to your eyes when exposed to cat dander?
questions.subtitle: Microscopic dander particles readily dissolve upon contact with eye membranes.

options.label: No eye irritation
options.description: Eyes remain clear and comfortable.

options.label: Occasional mild itchiness or slight watering
options.description: Minor sensitivity that resolves after washing hands and face.

options.label: Persistent itching, redness, and watery eyes
options.description: Intense urge to rub eyes, accompanied by stinging or clear discharge.

options.label: Severe swelling of eyelids, bloodshot redness, and burning pain
options.description: Significant conjunctival inflammation, puffiness, and photophobia.

questions.title: Respiratory & Airway Check
questions.question: Do you experience any coughing, chest tightness, or respiratory discomfort around cats?
questions.subtitle: Fel d 1 particles are less than 5 microns wide, allowing them to penetrate deep into pulmonary bronchioles.

options.label: None — no coughing or breathing discomfort
options.description: Your airways remain clear and unaffected.

options.label: Occasional mild cough or slight throat tickle
options.description: A minor dry throat tickle from airborne fur or dust, without breathing restriction.

options.label: Wheezing, chest tightness, or trouble breathing
options.description: A whistling breath sound, constriction in the chest, or shortness of breath.

questions.title: Skin & Contact Sensitivity
questions.question: How does your skin react to direct contact with cat fur, saliva, or licks?
questions.subtitle: Saliva contains the highest concentrations of Fel d 1, which transfers to skin upon contact.

options.label: No skin reaction
options.description: Petting, holding, or being licked causes zero marks or itching.

options.label: Occasional minor itch where licked or scratched
options.description: Faint local tingling that clears rapidly after washing with soap and water.

options.label: Noticeable redness, localized itchy welts, or blotches
options.description: Histamine flare-ups appearing at the exact point of feline contact.

options.label: Widespread hives (urticaria) or severe eczema flare-ups
options.description: Raised, intensely itchy welts spreading across arms, neck, or face.

questions.title: Treatment Responsiveness
questions.question: How do your symptoms respond to over-the-counter allergy relief?
questions.subtitle: How readily your histamine cascade responds to standard antihistamines or nasal sprays.

options.label: My symptoms are so mild I have never needed medication
options.description: Natural exposure causes minimal reaction without pharmaceutical intervention.

options.label: Standard OTC antihistamines provide fast, complete relief
options.description: A non-drowsy tablet or nasal spray rapidly clears symptoms.

options.label: I haven't tried allergy medication yet
options.description: You currently manage without medications and have not tested their efficacy.

options.label: Medication only partially takes the edge off
options.description: Antihistamines help slightly, but persistent irritation remains in the background.

options.label: Medications fail to relieve my symptoms
options.description: Standard oral medications provide virtually no relief from heavy dander exposure.

living_with_cat.summary: Your symptoms suggest mild sensitivity to cat allergens. Because you currently live with a cat, minor adjustments can keep you completely comfortable. Running a True HEPA air purifier in the bedroom, feeding an allergen-reducing diet to neutralize saliva Fel d 1, and regular HEPA vacuuming will dramatically reduce ambient dander levels.

thinking_of_adopting.summary: Your symptoms suggest mild sensitivity to cat allergens. If you are preparing to adopt, choosing a naturally low-Fel d 1 cat breed and setting up basic air filtration before adoption will help ensure a symptom-free transition.

living_with_cat.summary: Your symptoms suggest moderate sensitivity to cat allergens. To live comfortably with your cat, a multi-layered allergen reduction strategy is key: feed Purina LiveClear to neutralize saliva allergens, install True HEPA air cleaners, and keep cats out of your bedroom sanctuary.

thinking_of_adopting.summary: Your symptoms suggest moderate sensitivity to cat allergens. Before adopting, focus specifically on proven low-Fel d 1 breeds, schedule multiple in-person visits with breeders to test your personal reaction, and prepare your home with HEPA filtration.

living_with_cat.summary: Consult an allergist: Your symptoms suggest high sensitivity to cat allergens. Living with a cat while experiencing severe reactions requires intensive medical guidance. An allergist can evaluate you for prescription medications or allergen immunotherapy (allergy shots) alongside aggressive home filtration.

thinking_of_adopting.summary: Consult an allergist: Your symptoms suggest high sensitivity to cat allergens. Before committing to adoption, we strongly advise scheduling clinical allergy testing and consulting an allergist. You should only consider lower-Fel d 1 cats based on breeder lineage testing and published ratings (such as verified Siberians) and spend extended time with the specific cat beforehand.

red_flag.summary: You reported experiencing wheezing, chest tightness, coughing spells, or trouble breathing around cats. Lower respiratory symptoms can indicate feline-induced allergic asthma. Microscopic Fel d 1 proteins penetrate deep into lower bronchial airways, which can trigger dangerous bronchospasms. For your health and safety, please schedule an appointment with a physician or allergist for pulmonary evaluation. We do not provide product recommendations for respiratory conditions.
